land.text: Meknes, 'captured in 1244 or 1245', then Taza, Rabat, Salé and Fez by 1248

predecessors.note: Marrakesh followed in 1269; the page's header gives the dynasty as 1244-1465.

land.text: most of Morocco: the 1465 revolt 'led to the establishment of direct Wattasid rule over most of Morocco'; Muhammad ibn Yahya 'installs himself in Fez, where he founds the Wattasid dynasty' in 1472

successors.note: Between 1465 and 1472 Fez had a sharifian sultan, Muhammad ibn Ali Amrani-Joutey ('overthrown in 1471'); the Wattasid page gives 'Established: 1472'. Cliopatria's Wattasid row starts 1468.
Ceuta fell in 1415 and Ksar es-Seghir in 1458; Tangier in 1465 (Marinid page) or 1471 (Conquest of Ceuta page).

capitals.name: Fez
capitals.note: Text: after the capture of Fez in 1248 the Marinids 'made Fez their capital'; Fes Jdid was founded in 1276. Before 1248 the page names no seat. Marrakesh appears only as a conquest (1269).

rulers.name: Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Haqq
rulers.note: Chronology: 'Muhammad I is killed by an officer of his own Christian mercenary militia' (1244), Abu Yahya succeeded; died 1258. Earlier chiefs: Abd al-Haqq I (1215-1217), Abu Sa'id Uthman I (1217-1240), Abu Ma'ruf Muhammad I (1240-1244).

rulers.name: Abu Yusuf Yaqub
rulers.note: Infobox lists him 1269-1286; died at Algeciras in 1286 after a fourth expedition to Iberia.

rulers.name: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Uthman
rulers.note: The infobox list gives 1331-1351, the text 1331-1348; he died in May 1351 in his Atlas hideout (Abu al-Hasan page).

rulers.name: Abu Inan Faris al-Mutawakkil
rulers.note: Strangled by his vizier on 10 January 1358.

rulers.name: Abu Zian as-Said Muhammad ibn Faris
rulers.note: Named by the vizirs; a few months.

rulers.name: Abu Yahya Abu Bakr ibn Faris
Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz I ibn Ali
Abu al-Abbas Ahmad
rulers.note: Supported by the Nasrids; removed by them in 1384 and back in 1387 (to 1393).

rulers.name: Abu Faris Musa ibn Faris
rulers.note: Installed by the Nasrids in 1384; the page gives no end year.

rulers.name: Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz II ibn Ahmad
Abu Said Uthman III ibn Ahmad
Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq II
rulers.note: A one-year-old at his accession; under Wattasid vizirs; killed in the revolt of 1465.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1244-1247: Cliopatria's Marinid row starts in 1250. The page header gives the dynasty as 1244-1465 and 'Meknes was captured in 1244 or 1245'; Taza, Rabat and Salé fall between 1244 and 1248 (no year for each) and Fez in 1248. Only Meknes is certain for these years.

correction.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1248-1249: 'Between 1244 and 1248 the Marinids were able to take Taza, Rabat, Salé, Meknes and Fez from the weakened Almohads'; 'Fez was captured in 1248'. The year for Taza, Rabat and Salé is only the span.

correction.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws all of Morocco and a slice of the Algerian west (388,669 km2; 1,434 cells, the same cells as its 'Almohad Caliphate' rows of 1260-1343) for 1250-1259. The page has only Meknes, Taza, Rabat, Salé and Fez by 1248, Sijilmassa in 1255, Marrakesh in 1269 ('Seizure of Marrakesh and the end of Almohad domination of the western Maghreb'); the Almohads held Marrakesh and the south until then. The page has no area; the correction is the page-supported core, with Sijilmassa added by the ledger in 1255.

correction.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1260-1268, years Cliopatria files under 'Almohad Caliphate' with the Marinid shape: the page-supported core of 1250 (Marrakesh still Almohad until 1269; Sijilmassa 'in 1255' and again 'The Marinids seize Sijilmassa' in 1274). The Castilians raid Sale in 1260.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape of 1260, identical to its Marinid shape of 1250 and 1363, for 1269-1336

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1269-1336, the years Cliopatria files under 'Almohad Caliphate' (shapes 1260, 1285 and 1333, identical, 388,669 / 388,541 km2: Morocco and a slice of the Algerian west). Marrakesh falls in 1269 and the Marinids hold Morocco; the Souss and Draa are less certain (revolts 'around the Draa River and the province of Marrakesh' in 1286; 'Conquest and destruction of Taroudannt' in 1306). The page has no area. Iberian holdings (Rota, Tarifa, Gibraltar by 1294; Algeciras 1329-1344) and Ceuta (1309) are ledger events.

correction.text: Morocco and the conquered Kingdom of Tlemcen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1337-1343: Morocco plus the Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen, 'conquered' in May 1337 (Abu al-Hasan page; 'In 1337 the Abdalwadid kingdom of Tlemcen was conquered', Marinid page). Cliopatria shows the Marinid shape of 514,751 km2 only from 1344.

Cliopatria's 514,751 km2 shape (Morocco plus the Tlemcen kingdom) holds 1344-1347. The Zayyanids rule again at Tlemcen from 1348 to 1352 ('an interruption from 1348 to 1352'; Abu Said Uthman II and Abu Thabit I in the ruler table), so for 1348-1351 the Tlemcen part is wrong; the ledger records the end of the occupation in 1348 and its return in 1352. Ifriqiya is occupied from September 1347 to 1349 (ledger).

Cliopatria draws 737,941 km2 for 1352-1362: Morocco, all Algeria and Tunisia, and Tripolitania (the whole of Hafsid Ifriqiya). The pages give Tlemcen 1352-1359, Bejaia 1353 and Tunis only in 1357 ('forced to retreat from Tunisia in 1357'); Abu Inan was strangled on 10 January 1358 and 'a period of confusion followed' (the 'reign of the vizirs' to 1361). The correction is Morocco plus Tlemcen and Bejaia for 1352-1358; Morocco alone from 1359 (new keyframe marinid-sultanate_1359).
New keyframe for 1359-1362: 'Resurgence of the Zianids of Tlemcen' (1359) and Abu Hammu II restored in February 1359; the vizirs name sultans from 1358; Morocco alone.

388,541 km2, Morocco and a slice of the Algerian west. The page has no area. Within it: the third seizure of Tlemcen (1370), the partition into the Kingdoms of Fez and Marrakesh in 1374 (to 1387), the reconquest of 'Tlemcen and Algiers' in 1387; Henry III of Castile seized Tetouan in 1399 (a raid, 'massacring half the population'); the shape stands.

388,366 km2: Ceuta ('conquered ... from the Marinid Sultanate on 21 August 1415') leaves the shape, 175 km2 smaller than 1363. The Portuguese page has Abu Said Uthman III besiege Ceuta in 1419 (Marinid page: 1418) and fail.

Shape unchanged (388,366 km2) but it holds 1463-1465 only: 'The sultan was killed in the revolt, and Afonso V took Tangier' (1465); the Wattasid page: 'In 1465, Abd al-Haqq was killed during a revolt in Fez'; the row's 1467 end is Cliopatria's.

ledger.note: 1244: the Marinids take Meknes. The page header gives 'The Marinid sultanate 1244-1465' and 'Meknes was captured in 1244 or 1245'; Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Haqq rules 1244-1258 (the page's list). Earlier Marinid chiefs (Abd al-Haqq I, 1215-1217) fought the Almohads from the Rif coast with no territory recorded.

1244-1248: the Marinids take Taza, Rabat and Sale. 'Between 1244 and 1248 the Marinids were able to take Taza, Rabat, Sale, Meknes and Fez from the weakened Almohads'; the page gives the span, not a year each.
1248: the Marinids take Fez and make it their capital. 'Fez was captured in 1248', and the Marinids 'made Fez their capital'.
1248: the capital is Fez (the page gives 'established his capital in Fes' beside the 1248 capture).
1255: the Marinids take Sijilmassa. 'Fez was captured in 1248, and Sijilmassa in 1255.'

1269: the Marinids take Marrakesh and end Almohad rule. Chronology 'Seizure of Marrakesh and the end of Almohad domination of the western Maghreb'; the narrative: 'eventually succeeding in 1269 with the capture of Marrakesh'.

minus.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248

region.text: Cliopatria's Morocco without the places taken by 1248

ledger.note: 1269: the rest of Almohad Morocco (the Souss, the Draa, the Atlas) passes to the Marinids. Bridging: no page dates it; Cliopatria shows all Morocco Marinid from 1250 and the Almohad page leaves the last caliph 'reduced to Marrakesh'.
1274: the Marinids seize Sijilmassa again. Chronology 'The Marinids seize Sijilmassa.' The page does not say who held it after 1255; 'nobody' marks that no other dossier's state is named.
By 1294: the Marinids hold Rota, Tarifa and Gibraltar. 'By the year 1294 they had occupied Rota, Tarifa, and Gibraltar'; the page does not name the previous holder.
1299: the Marinids besiege Tlemcen. 'Beginning of Tlemcen's siege by the Marinids, which will last nine years.'
1306: Taroudannt is conquered and destroyed. Chronology 'Conquest and destruction of Taroudannt'; the page does not say whose it was.

1307: the siege of Tlemcen ends without conquest. 'After an eight-year siege of Tlemcen by the Marinids that ended in 1307' (the Marinid chronology says nine years); Abu Yaqub Yusuf an-Nasr is assassinated the same year.
1309: Abu al-Rabi Sulayman enters Ceuta. Chronology 'Abu al-Rabi Sulayman enters Ceuta'; the page does not name the previous holder.
1329: the Marinids beat the Castilians at Algeciras. Chronology 'The Marinids defeat the Castilians in Algeciras', 'gaining a foothold in southern Iberia'.

17 June 1333: Gibraltar surrenders to the Marinids. 'On 17 June 1333, Vasco Perez surrendered Gibraltar after agreeing terms with Abd al-Malik.' (Marinid page: 'after its reconquest from Christian forces in 1333').

May 1337: Abu al-Hasan takes Tlemcen. 'In May 1337, after a two-year siege, Tlemcen finally fell to a Marinid assault'; chronology '1337: First occupation of Tlemcen'; 'In 1337 the Abdalwadid kingdom of Tlemcen was conquered'. The page speaks of the city; the whole kingdom is the researcher's reading.

1344: the Marinids are 'definitively ejected from Iberia'. The chronology entry is about Algeciras; the general statement is the page's, the places (Rota, Tarifa, Gibraltar) are the researcher's reading.
March 1344: Castile takes Algeciras. 'Alfonso XI of Castile had little difficulty taking Algeciras in March 1344'; chronology 'The Castilians take over Algeciras'.

September 1347: Abu al-Hasan enters Tunis. 'In a campaign in early 1347, Abu al-Hasan's Moroccan army swept through Ifriqiya'; he 'entered Tunis in September 1347'; chronology 'destroys the Hafsid dynasty of Tunis and restores his authority over all the Maghreb'.

1348: Tlemcen is lost to the Zayyanids. The occupation of 1337 ran to 1348 ('with an interruption from 1348 to 1352'); chronology '1348: The Black Death and the rebellions of Tlemcen and Tunis mark the beginning of the decline of the Marinids'.
1349: Abu al-Hasan leaves Ifriqiya. 'Abu al-Hasan was forced to return west in 1349', the Arab tribes having defeated his army near Kairouan in April 1348.
1352: Abu Inan retakes Tlemcen. 'In 1352 Abu Inan Faris recaptured Tlemcen' (the chronology dates the 'Second seizure of Tlemcen' to 1351).
1353: Abu Inan takes Bejaia. 'He took Bejaia in 1353.'

August 1357: Abu Inan takes Tunis. He 'captured Tunis in August 1357, but he was soon forced by his own troops to abandon the region'. [Review af-02-d: month dropped and event placed before the 1357 retreat so that the start precedes its end; the month (August) stays in this note.]
1357: Abu Inan retreats from Tunisia. 'He was forced to retreat from Tunisia in 1357'; he fell ill in November 1357.
1358: Marinid Bejaia, bridging. The page gives no date for losing Bejaia; Abu Inan is strangled on 10 January 1358 and 'a period of confusion followed'.
1359: the Zayyanids are restored. 'A Marinid occupation of Tlemcen between 1337 and 1359'; chronology '1359: Resurgence of the Zianids of Tlemcen'.
1370: third seizure of Tlemcen (chronology '1370: Third seizure of Tlemcen'; the Zayyanid page: Marinid attempts 'up to 1370').
1372: Tlemcen is Zayyanid again, bridging. The Marinid page gives no end; the Zayyanid ruler table has Abu Hammu II back in 1372 (third reign).
1374: the sultanate is partitioned. Chronology 'Partition of the empire into two kingdoms: the Kingdom of Fez and the Kingdom of Marrakesh'.
1387: the Kingdom of Marrakesh ends. 'Abu Zayd Abd ar-Rahman reigns over the Kingdom of Marrakesh from 1384 to 1387' while the throne remained in Fez; the page gives no reunification event.
1387: Abu al-Abbas reconquers Tlemcen and Algiers. Chronology '1387: ... he reconquered Tlemcen and Algiers'; the page does not date any later retreat.
1389: Zayyanid rule again, bridging. The Marinid page is silent; the Zayyanid ruler table has Abu Hammu II to 1389 (fifth and final reign) and Abu Tashufin II from 1389.
21 August 1415: Portugal takes Ceuta. John I 'conquered the North African city of Ceuta from the Marinid Sultanate on 21 August 1415'; the Marinids besiege it in 1419 and fail.

1458: Portugal takes Ksar es-Seghir. The Conquest of Ceuta page: 'the taking of Ksar es-Seghir (1458), Arzila and Tangier (1471)'; the Marinid chronology: Afonso V 'used it to attack a small port between Tangier and Ceuta'.
1465: Afonso V takes Tangier. Chronology: the sultan 'was killed in the revolt, and Afonso V took Tangier'; the Conquest of Ceuta page dates Arzila and Tangier to 1471.

1465: a revolt in Fez kills the last Marinid sultan. 'Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Haqq appoints a Jewish vizir, Aaron ben Batash, provoking a popular revolt'; 'In 1465, Abd al-Haqq was killed during a revolt in Fez' (Wattasid page), which 'led to the establishment of direct Wattasid rule over most of Morocco'; Fez had a sharifian sultan until 1471 and the Wattasids 'install' themselves in 1472.

wars.name: Marinid conquest of Morocco

zones.text: Meknes, Fez, Taza, Rabat and Salé, the places the Marinids took from the Almohads in 1244-1248

wars.outcome: Marinid victory: Meknes 1244 or 1245, Taza, Rabat and Sale by 1248, Fez 1248, Sijilmassa 1255, Marrakesh 1269.

wars.name: Marinid siege of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Indecisive: the siege of eight or nine years ends in 1307 without a conquest.

wars.name: Marinid campaigns in Iberia
wars.outcome: Marinid footholds (Rota, Tarifa and Gibraltar by 1294; Algeciras from 1329; Gibraltar retaken 17 June 1333) end with the defeat at Rio Salado (October 1340) and the fall of Algeciras (March 1344).
wars.note: The Marinids were allied with the Emirate of Granada (peace treaty of Fez, 26 February 1334, between Castile, Granada and Morocco).

wars.name: Marinid conquest of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Marinid victory: invasion early 1335, siege broken off 1336 or 1337, Tlemcen falls in May 1337.

wars.name: Marinid invasion of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Initial victory (Tunis, September 1347), then defeat by the Arab tribes near Kairouan (April 1348) and withdrawal in 1349.

wars.name: Abu Inan's campaigns
wars.outcome: Tlemcen 1352, Bejaia 1353, Tunis August 1357, all lost with his death on 10 January 1358.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Ceuta
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory on 21 August 1415; the Marinid siege of 1419 (1418 in the Marinid chronology) fails.

wars.name: Portuguese expeditions against Tangier and Ksar es-Seghir
wars.outcome: The 1437 expedition to Tangier fails; Ksar es-Seghir falls in 1458 and Tangier in 1465 (Conquest of Ceuta page: 1471).

certainty.note: No treaty line is given for any Marinid frontier: the Moulouya frontier with Tlemcen, the Saharan edge and the Atlas are approximate; the peace of Fez in February 1334 between Castile, Granada and Morocco is a truce, not a line. Ceuta and Gibraltar are firm points.

notes: CLIOPATRIA. (1) The Marinid row has a hole 1260-1343 and 'Almohad Caliphate' carries the Marinid shape (1,434 cells, identical to the Marinid shapes of 1250 and 1363) for those years: this dossier reviews the Marinid row only but adds new keyframes for 1269-1336 and 1337-1343 that point at the Almohad rows' shape. (2) The 1250 shape gives the Marinids all Morocco from 1250; the page has only Meknes, Taza, Rabat, Sale and Fez by 1248, Sijilmassa 1255 and Marrakesh 1269. (3) The 1352-1362 shape (737,941 km2) covers all Hafsid land and is wrong: the pages give the Marinids Tlemcen 1352-1359, Bejaia 1353-1358 and Tunis for months of 1357. (4) The row ends 1467, the page 1465, the Wattasid page 1472 (with a sharifian interlude 1465-1471). AREA. The Marinid page has no infobox dates or area figure; no comparison was possible. NOT SETTLED. The Souss, the Draa and the Atlas before 1306; who held Sijilmassa 1255-1274, Taroudannt, Ceuta (1309) and Rota, Tarifa and Gibraltar (1294) before the Marinids (recorded as 'nobody' or crown-of-castile where the page is silent); Marinid control of Tlemcen and Algiers 1387-1389 and 1370-1372 (ends bridged from the Zayyanid ruler table); the Marinid suzerainty of Granada; the Castilian raids on Sale (1260) and Tetouan (1399); the Almohad infobox's 'Marinid suzerainty: 1248'. Rulers: the page's chronology and infobox list; the infobox and text disagree on Abu al-Hasan (1351 or 1348) and Abd al-Aziz I (1365 or 1366); the end of Abu Faris Musa's interim (1384) is not given. COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: 'Marinid Kingdom of Marrakesh' (1374-1387, internal); the sharifian sultanate of Fez of Muhammad ibn Ali Amrani-Joutey (1465-1471; successor not given a slug); wattasid-dynasty is the group's other batch.
